# Clay/Stars PHP transform fixtures

These are **synthetic unit-test inputs**, not a captured WordPress page, an approved
release payload, or evidence that a live site renders correctly.

`base.html` exercises the legacy content shape: one atmosphere, one cover, one
player, five chapter controls, links, readable text, a superseded motion script,
and an unrelated script. `expected.html` is a separately authored golden output:
three decorative cover spans, one cloud field, and only the superseded script
removed. It is not generated by the production filter during a test run.

`manifest.json` pins both files' SHA-256 digests. The loader accepts CRLF checkouts
only by mapping CRLF back to LF; all other bytes are preserved. Missing files,
changed text, invalid UTF-8, null/replacement bytes, and added BOM bytes fail.
Review changes to both HTML and the manifest together; never refresh the golden
output or hashes just to make a failing test green.

The PHP tests load the actual plugin entrypoint with a small WordPress context
stub. They run without WordPress, media downloads, generated `qa/` pages or any
external release directory. All checks use explicit booleans and exit codes,
not PHP `assert()` settings.

Run from the repository root:

```sh
php tests/validate-clay-transform.php
php tests/validate-clay-legacy-collision.php
node tests/clay-transform-fixtures.test.cjs
```

The regular `tools/validate.ps1 -Mode Unit` already discovers the new Node test
and runs both PHP tests; no preparation command or validator bypass is required.
The Node test needs the same `php` executable on PATH as the Unit coordinator.
It can also use `PHP_BINARY` when invoked directly.

For the separate, explicit release-payload comparison and acceptance boundaries,
see [Clay transform validation](../../../docs/clay-transform-validation.md).
